title: Amanara Residence: 24 duplex villas a road from Bandar Utama.
videoTitle: PROPERTY REVIEW #430 | AMANARA RESIDENCE, KAYU ARA
excerpt: A boutique block of 24 duplex units of about 2,000 sq ft from RM1.5 million, in a kampung area one road from Bandar Utama, offering something between a condo and a landed home.
takeaways: Only 24 duplex units of about 2,000 sq ft, from RM1.5 million, two per lift landing.
6 m wide living spaces, 3.5 m ceilings and big windows, with basic facilities.
Narrow kampung roads, noise for front units, and similar boutique projects likely on neighbouring plots.

sections.heading: What sets it apart
paragraphs: Amanara has just 24 duplex units on leasehold land, each about 2,000 sq ft with three bedrooms, three bathrooms, a powder room and two tandem car parks. One lift serves two units per landing. Lower units have living space below and bedrooms above, like a landed home; upper units, the one Sean toured, have the living floor above and bedrooms downstairs.

The living floor is 6 m wide with 3.5 m ceilings and windows across the facade, and the kitchen is about 3 m wide with cross ventilation. The master bedroom is 4.9 by 4.2 m. Facilities are minimal: a gym and games room in two ground-floor units and a small playground. Prices start from about RM1.5 million.

sections.heading: Where it is
paragraphs: The project is in Kampung Sungai Kayu Ara, between the LDP and the road to the NKVE, one street from Bandar Utama and Centrepoint, near the coming LRT3 line. Kampung houses still surround it, with narrow roads, overhead cables and double parking, and a mosque at the end of the road busy at Friday prayers. Shops and eateries are a short walk away.

sections.heading: Rent and returns
paragraphs: This furnished unit is asking about RM6,500 a month, which Sean says would justify the price if achieved. He still sees Amanara mainly as an own-stay product, noting that the neighbouring block is almost fully occupied.

pros: An alternative in a prime area: between a RM400,000-plus condo and a RM1.8 to 2 million link house in Bandar Utama, a step before upgrading to landed, with only 24 neighbours you will likely all know.
The unit: a 6 m width, 3.5 m ceilings, big rooms, big windows, good bathrooms and solid materials. Lower units are the more popular, as they feel more like a landed home.
A location in transition: one road from mature Bandar Utama, with LRT3, highways and multinationals nearby, as the kampung slowly redevelops.
cons: The micro site: narrow kampung roads, double parking and congestion. Neighbouring plots will likely become similar duplex projects, which means competition at RM1.6 to 1.8 million.
Site limits: front units hear the road, the RFID entrance is basic, visitor parking is scarce, and each unit gets only two tandem bays. Placing the gym and games room nearest the road helps.
Uncoordinated structure: old-style beams and columns leave awkward corners, beams and level drops inside, though interior design can hide them.

closing: Sean says he wouldn't mind owning one: at RM1.2 million he wouldn't think twice, and at RM1.5 million he would think about it.
sourceNote: Based on Sean's full English captions for this March 2026 episode. The 3 on 3 follows the three things he likes and the three he doesn't, in his order, at the end of the video. An owner let Sean view a unit furnished by The Makeover Guys, a furnishing company Sean works with, and he also saw an empty unit as handed over.
